title: A Pot of Tea
cardDescription: Tea types, pot parts, and familiar words for brewing a cup.
description: Settle in with a tea-themed crossword about familiar teaware, the leaves inside a cup, and the words used to describe brewing.
focus: The clues cover tea, its containers, and the small accessories used in making it. Some words name a whole vessel, while others name a part or a small item. Direct definitions point to each item's everyday use.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a tea type, a whole container, a part, or an accessory. The vessel that heats water and the one used to brew and serve tea have different names. Short accessory words can help cross longer teaware terms.

answerNotes.TEAPOT: A teapot is used for brewing and serving tea. Its spout is the pouring part, while a saucer is a separate dish beneath a cup.
answerNotes.KETTLE: A kettle heats the water before tea is made. It may be heated on a stove or have an electric heating element; the clue names the vessel's job.
answerNotes.STEEP: Steep is a brewing verb here: leave plant material in water to draw out flavor. It does not describe the slope of a hill.
answerNotes.INFUSE: Infuse describes drawing flavor from material into a liquid. In this setting it is a brewing action rather than a particular tea variety.
answerNotes.STRAINER: A tea strainer catches loose leaves while the liquid passes through. It names the utensil, not the leaves or the pot.
answerNotes.SAUCER: A saucer is the small dish beneath a cup. It differs from the cup that actually holds the drink.
answerNotes.SPOUT: The spout is the projecting pouring part. The handle is where the vessel is held, so the two parts serve different purposes.
answerNotes.OOLONG: Oolong tea is partially oxidized during processing. The degree varies, so it is a tea category rather than one fixed flavor.
answerNotes.DARJEELING: Darjeeling is a place name used for tea from that growing region of India. The clue asks for the regional name rather than one piece of teaware.

title: Morning Coffee Words
cardDescription: Coffee preparation, aroma, and familiar additions to a morning mug.
description: Wake up a few familiar words with a crossword about coffee beans, brewing, and the everyday language of a morning mug.
focus: This puzzle follows coffee from the bean to the cup. Some clues ask for a material or a tool, while others describe preparation, aroma, or something added at the table. Familiar coffee words have more specific meanings in this setting.
solvingTip: Look for the difference between a whole bean, the material after grinding, and the finished drink. A word may describe an action or something the drink contains. Short preparation and serving words can help with longer coffee terms.

answerNotes.BEAN: Coffee beans are botanically seeds. Bean is the familiar everyday name used in buying and preparing coffee.
answerNotes.ROAST: Roast means heat the beans to develop flavor and color. Grinding is a different step that makes the beans into smaller particles.
answerNotes.GROUNDS: Grounds is a plural noun for the crushed coffee material. In this clue it refers to what remains in the filter, not an area of land.
answerNotes.FILTER: A coffee filter lets liquid through while holding back particles. The word identifies the separating material rather than the finished beverage.
answerNotes.DECAF: Decaf is short for decaffeinated. Much of the caffeine has been removed, but the word does not necessarily mean completely caffeine-free.
answerNotes.CAFFEINE: Caffeine is naturally present in regular coffee. The clue identifies the substance without prescribing an amount to consume.
answerNotes.PERK: Perk is an informal coffee-brewing verb associated with a percolator. It can also mean become more cheerful or name an extra benefit in another setting.
answerNotes.BLEND: A coffee blend combines coffees from different sources. It names the mixture rather than the act of grinding or a particular serving vessel.

title: A Warm Cup of Cocoa
cardDescription: Chocolate ingredients, gentle mixing words, and sweet finishing touches.
description: Picture a warm cup of cocoa while solving clues about chocolate ingredients, mixing words, and familiar toppings.
focus: The clues focus on ingredients, their forms, and actions associated with a cup of cocoa. Some answers describe the drink or its surface; others name a flavoring or a topping. The definitions supply vocabulary rather than a complete recipe.
solvingTip: Look for a mixing action, a serving vessel, or a topping. A thin chocolate sliver differs from the bubbles on the drink's surface. Short action and serving words can help cross the longer topping names.

answerNotes.COCOA: Cocoa powder is made from cacao solids after much of the cocoa butter has been removed. It differs from a prepared sweetened drink mix that may contain other ingredients.
answerNotes.FROTH: Froth is a collection of small bubbles at a liquid's surface. It names the bubbly layer rather than a dry powder sprinkled over it.
answerNotes.MARSHMALLOW: A marshmallow is a soft, spongy confection. The singular form names one sweet, even when several small ones float on a drink.
answerNotes.CINNAMON: Cinnamon is a bark spice. Nutmeg comes from a seed, giving a different source for another familiar warm-drink flavor.
answerNotes.VANILLA: Vanilla traditionally comes from cured orchid pods. The clue uses that source to identify the flavoring.
answerNotes.NUTMEG: Nutmeg is a seed used as a spice and often grated. The clue asks for the spice name rather than a whole nut eaten as a snack.
answerNotes.MELT: Melt describes changing a solid into liquid with heat. Stirring moves the mixture around and is a different action.
answerNotes.SHAVING: A shaving is a very thin sliver in this food context. The word describes a piece cut from chocolate rather than an action involving facial hair.
answerNotes.CURL: Curl names a curved decoration here. Its shape distinguishes it from fine powder or a flat piece of chocolate.

title: At the Diner Counter
cardDescription: Diner seating, coffee refills, and familiar American breakfast words.
description: Step up to a familiar American diner for a crossword about counter seating, coffee service, and breakfast words.
focus: This puzzle looks at the setting around a cup of diner coffee. Clues name places to sit, service words, and familiar breakfast items. American restaurant usage supplies the intended meaning for words that also occur in other settings.
solvingTip: Look for whether the clue asks for seating, something on the table, a service word, or a food. An extra serving of coffee and an extra payment for service have different names. Short table and breakfast words can help cross longer diner terms.

answerNotes.COUNTER: A diner counter is the long serving surface faced by seated customers. The clue uses a restaurant fixture, not a device that counts things.
answerNotes.BOOTH: A restaurant booth has fixed bench seating around a table. It differs from a stool placed along an open counter.
answerNotes.CHECK: Check is a common American restaurant word for the bill. The clue asks for that service use rather than an inspection or a bank payment.
answerNotes.TIP: A tip is an additional payment for service in this setting. It is distinct from the meal's listed charges on the check.
answerNotes.REFILL: A refill is another serving added to a cup after the first has been drunk. The word combines re-, meaning again, with fill.
answerNotes.CARAFE: A carafe is a serving vessel for pouring a drink. It names the container rather than the cup from which a guest drinks.
answerNotes.OMELET: Omelet is a common American spelling for the folded egg dish. Omelette is another accepted spelling, so the crossing letters matter.
answerNotes.WAFFLE: A waffle gets its grid pattern from the cooking iron. The clue identifies the food rather than the verb meaning to hesitate.

title: Lemonade on the Porch
cardDescription: Citrus parts, garnishes, and simple pouring words.
description: Enjoy a porch-side crossword about citrus fruits, garnishes, and everyday words for serving lemonade.
focus: The clues describe citrus parts and words associated with serving a cold drink. Some answers name a piece of fruit or a garnish, while others describe an action or a quality. Familiar meanings guide the solving without requiring recipe measurements.
solvingTip: Decide whether the clue asks for a fruit part, a shape, or an action. A thin round piece and a thicker pointed segment have different names. Short serving words can help with longer drink terms.

answerNotes.PITCHER: Pitcher is the familiar American serving-container word in this clue. It also names a baseball player, but the spout and handle identify the household meaning.
answerNotes.CUBE: Cube names the small block shape here. It is a shape word rather than the material, which is ice.
answerNotes.SLICE: Slice is a noun here for a thin flat piece. The word can also be a verb for cutting such pieces, so the clue asks for the object rather than the action.
answerNotes.WEDGE: A wedge is a pointed segment rather than a thin round slice. The clue asks for the shape of the cut piece.
answerNotes.RIND: Rind is an outer fruit covering. Zest refers more specifically to the colored outermost part of citrus skin used for flavor.
answerNotes.ZEST: Zest names the colored outermost citrus skin in this food context. The pale layer beneath it is called pith.
answerNotes.MINT: Mint is an aromatic herb here. The same word can name a place that makes coins, but the garnish setting selects the plant meaning.
answerNotes.STRAW: Straw is the hollow drinking tube in this clue. It does not refer to dried grain stalks used as bedding.
answerNotes.TART: Tart is an adjective describing a sharp sour taste here. The same spelling can also name a small pastry, which is a different meaning.
